steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ How many custom sprite image assets should be found in My Assets?


Solution:

The spriteImage0 asset should be duplicated 3 times, then customized to create 4 unique sprite image assets. The 3 new assets should be added to the spriteImages array.


Ask the ninja: 

❓ What should the new value of the currentTile be set to, after the existing tiles have been replaced?


Solution:

The value of the currentTile variable should be reassigned to the element at the newIndex value of the pathTiles array, at the bottom of the changeScene function definition.

Ask the ninja: 

❓ What variable value determines which set of assets are displayed on screen?


Solution:

An if/else conditional should be added above the function call, inside the B button pressed event, that checks if currentIndex is equal to 3. If so, currentIndex should be set to 0, else it should increase by 1.
steps.instructions:
Fix the bugs in the code to create a working project!


The project should cycle through 4 unique sprite images, each time the B button is pressed.


The tilemap tiles should change every time the B button is pressed.


After the fourth background image, tile, and sprite image are displayed, the project should display the first set of assets found in the background, tile, and sprite image arrays. 


Use the functions in the code menu and the code completion tool to create a working version of this project!

subgroups.title: Debugging Cycling through Assets
subgroups.introduction: Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!

validationItems.failureText: Try rereading the instructions, then updating the code to create a working project.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 4 of Brown Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about pixel art and how to use the asset editor to modify an existing asset. You will also use code from the Scroller and Images categories to enrich the project. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 4:

badges.title: Remixologist
badges.description: Use the paint editor to modify and remix existing pixel art image assets.

badges.title: Doppelganger
badges.description: Edit an existing asset to create multiple versions of the same image.

badges.title: Nice Change of Scenery
badges.description: Use the Scroller extension to create a background that scrolls and changes images as a sprite “walks”.

badges.title: Swatch and Learn
badges.description: Write code to get, set, and replace a pixel’s color on an image asset.

badges.title: A Refined Palette
badges.description: Use RGB values or hex color code to change the colors of the code editor’s color palette.

badges.title: Mixing it Up
badges.description: Use the Color Palette tool to change the default color palette with different colors.
